messages.text:
"You are building a high-fidelity remake of the classic 2007 Java ME game \"Kamikaze Robots\".

Match the feel, visuals, and mechanics of the original as closely as possible based on the following detailed observations from the classic version.

GAME FEEL @COMMENT_BODY@ FLOW
- 2D side-scrolling tumbling racer.
- The robot is launched from the top of a slope by a digger arm after a clear 3-2-1 countdown.
- Camera follows the robot. Terrain, planets, black hole, asteroids, and stars scroll at different speeds (strong parallax).
- Distance is tracked in meters on the HUD.
- A pale blue ghost robot represents the player's best run and moves along the course.
- Checkpoints appear as banners (e.g. \"CHECKPOINT 1: METEORS\", \"CHECKPOINT 2: MOON\").

CORE PHYSICS – BOUNCE POWER SYSTEM (CRITICAL – MUST BE PRECISE)
- The robot continuously tumbles clockwise while moving forward.
- Hold the action button (Fire / F / touch) to apply brake force and control spin/orientation.
- Bounce power is determined by the quality of the landing and the number of spins completed after a good takeoff:

  - Feet-first landing → normal base jump.
  - If the robot completes 1 full spin in the air after a feet-first jump and lands on its feet again → jump power increases by \~0.2.
  - If it completes 2 full spins before the next feet-first landing → jump power increases by an additional \~0.3 on top of the previous boost.
  - Further consecutive spins before a feet-first landing continue to stack the power in a similar incremental way.
  - The instant the first contact with the ground is any part other than the feet → bounce power resets to base.
  - Bad landings (body, head, arms, or legs hitting first) produce only a very small bounce (roughly 0.5 to 1 robot length high) and do not grant power stacking.

- Good landings should make the robot spring forward and upward in a bent-legged pose, never launching backward.
- The Fire key / action button lights up near successful landings. Successful boosts are accompanied by yellow sparkles and a clear increase in speed.

LIMB LOSS @COMMENT_BODY@ HEAD LAUNCH
- Bad landings (non-feet-first contact) cause the robot to lose limbs.
- Limb loss order: arms first, then legs.
- Higher Stamina upgrades increase resistance (more bad hits required before a limb detaches).
- When all four limbs are gone and only the body remains:
  - On the next ground contact, the head is launched as a projectile.
  - Launch direction matches the direction the body is currently pointing at the moment of impact.
- Detached limbs should fall away visually.

TERRAIN @COMMENT_BODY@ LEVEL DESIGN
- Ground colliders must perfectly match the visual silhouette of the terrain (including edges, small bumps, and slopes). No floating or clipping.
- Levels must be longer and harder than typical short builds. Include varied terrain, slopes, gaps, and obstacles.
- Visual details observed in the original: rocket flame trail at high speed, red-outlined slopes, electric sparks, meteors, moon, black hole, planets, and asteroids.

UPGRADE SYSTEM
- Collectible chips grant upgrades: Jump, Spin, Stamina, Explosion.
- Progression must be relatively slow so the robot does not become overpowered too quickly compared to AI opponents or the challenge of the course.
- Tournament structure with distance objectives and chip rewards.

CONTROLS
- Automatic forward momentum + continuous clockwise spin.
- Hold to brake (slows spin and gives directional control).
- Must work well with both keyboard (space / F) and mobile touch.

VISUAL STYLE
- Pixel-art / retro Java ME aesthetic matching the original as closely as possible.
- Clear visual feedback for power level, successful boosts (sparkles), limb loss, and head launch.
- Parallax background layers (stars, planets, black hole, asteroids).

TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
- Clean, modular code.
- Reliable physics (frame-rate independent where practical).
- Support desktop and mobile from the start.
- Include main menu, player ready screen, and tournament/level selection.
- Distance counter, checkpoint system, and best-run ghost.

Start by implementing the core robot, precise bounce power stacking system (spins + feet-first landings), launch sequence with digger arm, and one complete longer level that demonstrates all the mechanics. Make everything modular so additional courses and upgrades can be added later.

Ask clarifying questions if any mechanic is ambiguous before implementing.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"
